facts.text: Brookfield was named after a city in England, with land set aside for a village green and cemetery in public trust forever.
Judge Samuel Hinckley bought 15,305 acres in 1798 through the Connecticut Land Company lottery, founding Brookfield.
Brookfield’s historic society at 6844 Strimbu Drive preserves archives and hosts lectures that keep the township’s legacy alive.
The award‑winning Yankee Run Golf Course, open March to October, earned national praise from Golf Digest and Ohio Magazine for its scenic layout.
Brookfield’s early settlers included trappers, missionaries, and Delaware Native Americans who called the area Menshadowa Crebo, meaning “land of many springs.”.
Brookfield’s founding values—land stewardship, civic trust, and neighborly cooperation—continue to shape the community today.
